reviews.review:
SCORE 8/10

It was an enjoyable and unique game. It definitely makes you consider our current surveillance in the world and how it's all headed to exactly what George Orwell predicted in 1984. There is a LOT of reading, so if that is not your thing, then this game is absolutely not for you. I wish it had more replayability and I wish it was longer.
When I purchased this game, I didn't realise it was a single story. That said, the story was very engaging and I found the game to be a lot of fun.

Well what can I say.... I really enjoyed the game and wish it was longer with other campaigns or something like that! It is really structured well and you have all the decisions, I found it difficult sometimes to think what is right or wrong - I will definatley be playing this game again and again to find different outcomes! I really enjoyed it and would recommend it :)
The games give a dystopian view on the [strike]future[/strike] present. It's only shortcoming is that it's rather short.
Very thought provoking.
A suprisingly effective adventure game with a novel interface. Some of the story progression was a bit confusing to me, but overall quite good.  Not long, but reasonably priced for what you get.

Amazing experience, very immersive - got me suprisingly hooked.
Near the end I wasn't paying as much attention, which lead me to a "wait - what am i doing again?" kind of moment, but overall it's worth a play.

This is an excellent game.  I went into it fully expecting it to be about the evils of government surveillance, and that you would see first hand the terrible effects and repercussions that it will bring.  Instead I got a very nuanced storyline that presented both sides of the issue, leaving you wondering afterwards if perhaps there is a practical middle ground that can be sought.  The gameplay is also very addictive and unique, and there are several endings depending on your choices, with lots of little twists and turns.  The game is very intelligent in regards to making your choices make a huge difference in the outcome, even if you think the ones you pick are not that important in the grand scheme of things.  One of the best titles I played this past year. Highly recommended.
Nice, immersive game for a sunday afternoon - if you are happy with reading a lot of texts and snoop around in other people's lifes, that's the game for you

[h1] "Thoughts Are Meant To Be Free" [/h1]

[b] DISCLAIMER - As of the time i am writing this review, i only played through one ending. [/b]

As soon as i finished the game, i had the urge to write this review, the urge to share with the world how amazingly complex and mind-boggling this game is.
Orwell in a way reminded me of [i] Papers, Please [/i] (Which you can find my review of it [url=http://steamcommunity.com/id/theaceshoelace/recommended/239030/] HERE [/url]).

In Orwell you will be The Big Brother. You will snoop into people's lives and find some and some less sensitive information about said people.
Orwell Does not contain much gameplay, Yet it succeeds to be an amazing piece of art, Solely with it's story.



Do i recommend Orwell?[b] Absolutely.[/b]

It's amazing. It's unique. [b] It's not for everyone. [/b]
I won't recommend it though, for people who get bored easily, and look for gameplay and graphics rather than story.

[h1] EDIT : [/h1]

So now that i managed to do all endings and basically turn the game inside out for the achievements, it's safe to say this game is a 10/10. 

Every single conflict you'll encounter will guarantee to have an impact on the way the story goes, making you really question which one to add to the database.

There are numerous endings, each one has it's own consequences and effects on The Nation (Where the game takes place).

As said earlier, get it only if you're a nut for a good, solid storyline. Otherwise, don't bother with it.

<3333333333333333333333333333333

If you find George Orwell's work to be amazing, you will love this.
this game was bien
Awesome writing, there were moments I actually felt like I was spying on a real conversation. The game play was enjoyable, and the story fascinating. 10/10 Would be an Orwell spy again!

>Have innocent person arrested
>Her lawyer tries to get her out of jail
>Have him arrested as well
>Have some hard-working single mother arrested
>Have my boss arrested
>Have myself arrested
>Still can't stop the terrorists

9/10 would become a national disgrace/fugitive again
Fantastic story driven game, Simplistic, yet fun. Defintely worth your time to experience.

This game is exciting in the quietest possible way.

I have not finished the game, but feel I have been allowed to guide the story's progress without having a full or obvious window on how I am doing so. 

Narrative and engaging at surprising pace.

Well I can safely say that this game proves that playing a game is different then watching one get played. The choice of what to upload is up to you. (Though somethings must be uploaded to make progress) The act of making those calls is what gives this game weight. That and the impact on the characters. This is a timely reminder of a possible near future where too much freedom is given up for security. Provided you don't mind doing a bunch of reading and not just uploading everything I can safely recommend this game. 

Not much re-playability but thought provoking and does not over stay its welcome.

Thoughtful, innovative game. Tells a complex story, largely successfully.   


Inability to correct mistakes is somewhat annoying - an 'undo' button would be nice - but it's obvious why the design choice was made that way.   

It's seems that not everything can be revealed on the first playthrough, but replayability is low: several scenes play out over minutes of time, which is fun the first time but boring the second.  I'd like to make different decisions on a second playthrough, but don't have the patience to sit through it all again.

A nice tight game with a moral dillema in its core which is most relevan right now. Do we allow the "Orwellian" distopia to occur to stop criminals?

you play as "The bad guy" investigating a bombing, eventually uncovering a disturbing truth about it.

even though the game is short and dumbed down somewhat (extracting data packets is your main job), you get to have some say in how the story goes, especially near the end.

Eventhough the game is short, its still has an engaging story with good writing and a unique feel.

Replaying a story-driven little-actual-gameplay game is a rare occurrence for me, let alone replaying it immediately after the first time, and yet I did it here since I felt that it would have enough replayability to stand up, and it did. 

Chats and phone calls move fast enough to make adding datachunks awkward, but too slow otherwise, especially the second time through them when you already know what everyone is going to say. While one conversation is under a time limit, the rest could use a fast-forward button.

The game is very short. I have 6 hours on record and that's from playing through the game in its entirety twice, including some idle time when I walked away from the computer. Some players may not find the amount of content acceptable considering the price.

By far the biggest issue is that [spoiler]Orwell is essentially introduced and dismantled within the game world during the course of the game. While that is obviously relevant to the plot and its general message, I can't help but feel that there's potential for multiple cases using this "engine", for lack of a better word, so it's a shame that, narratively, that can't occur,[/spoiler] although the fact that I find that in particular to be the largest issue is a very good thing for this game.
One of the most compellingly written and thought provoking narratives I've ever experienced. Please, please, please make greater use of this engine in the future and give us some new stories with it!

Honestly I loved this game. You have to make some difficult choices in-game that have difficult consiquenses. This game made me feel like I was doing something important, like I was effecting these people. I do have a tendency to really get immersed in what I'm playing (especially with games like these), but I feel like it wouldnt be that hard for anyone to do in this game. Overall, I would absolutly recomend Orwell to anyone.

I played around with the demo for a while before I bought this game and I have to say, I don't regret it.
The game gave me POI vibes and I love that show a lot, so that's a plus. Gameplay is simple, but the story is engaging, as well as the art. I don't mind playing through it all over again.
PS. Looking forward to season 2!

An outstanding narratively-focused game.  Don't go into it expecting a simulation of being at the reigns of an Orwellian state--it's not quite that--it's an interesting story that's driven by privacy-invading investigation.  It kind of gave me Phoenix Wright vibes in that there's a strong story hidden behind layers that have to be carefully peeled back.  There's varying outcomes and multiple endings depending on which information you choose to pass along.

Anyone with a Facebook page should play this. Great commentary on the age of the internet where privacy may very well be just an illusion we feed ourselves. It's also an interesting twist on the idea of a power fantasy. You don't have big guns or magic powers, you have personal information of everyone at your finger tips. And information is power no?

Be prepared tho for a somewhat guided experience. To keep the story in line, there are only chosen lines of text that you can pick out, but you still have the power to pick whether or not you include some of them. Main issue I have with this otherwise smart game is that it's a little difficult to keep track find data you chose to not pick out because you previously thought it wasn't relevant. And it's kinda hard to tell what data will move the story forward vs what is data that you can leave out to change the outcome.

Orwell had me on the edge of my seat the entire playthrough, even though there's no actual action going on on the screen. The story is magnificent. There's a few great plot twists in between the meat of the narrative, which is focused on making you think about freedom and security. Realizing that my actions, which weren't more than reading some text and dragging some info, had real consequences, I was completely engrossed in the game. Great stuff!

Loved the game, great story and very intuitive to play.
It makes you think about the surveillance society we possibly might be living under without knowing about it.

Price of €10 might seem a bit steep, but if you are into a good story and a bit of "hacking" you'll love this game for sure!

If you like interactive stories, this game is definitely one worth checking out! While this is all fictional the game does provide a lot to think of when it comes to our presence online as well as measures that are taken for safety.

I bought the game on sale for 8€ and finished the story within 4hrs.

Pros:

+Important and contemporary message in the light of NSA scandals and the demise of privacy in general.
+Choice matters
+Original gameplay offers a new take on the genre of text adventures.
+Nice interface
+Unique design


Cons:

-The hacking and surveilance parts are way off. In a game like this I would've hoped for more realism.
-Even though choice matters you're being guided by your supervisor in the game. You can withhold information from him but whenever I felt like doing that it was a piece of information mandatory for the story to continue. At 2-way story-forks the most interesting option often was missing I felt, which again lead to the feeling of being railroaded.
-Almost every bit of information you put into the system is commented by a pop-up comment of your supervisor which becomes a nuisance rather quickly.


Conclusion:

I really wanted to like this game. The theme of George Orwells "1984" is more relevant than ever. However I feel like the games tries too hard to hammer home their point of everybody being "frameable" by using one unforseeable plot-twist after another, which again is due to the supervisor railroading you. Also I would rather pay like 5€ more and have the tapped phone calls be actual phone calls instead of reading through live transcipts.

Concept : Good
Execution: Great
Story: Good
Characters: Good except for one who was difficult to empathize with.
Ending: Felt rushed and somewhat ham-fisted, but maybe I just chose a poorly written ending.

The game is really less a detective game than an [b]interactive story[/b].

My main disappointment is, you don't investigate in this game, not until the very end.
You end up following a story, told by a frustrating colleague of yours. From the start, to the end, he is [b][i]always[/i] telling you what to do[/b]. Please game, stop holding my hand. I had the feeling the game was playing for me most of the time. So, there is limited choice throughout most of the game...

... But it still has some "that thing may have not happened if I chose that instead of this an hour ago" moments. I'll certainly play again. One huge downside is, you can't go back to a specific chapter, if you want to replay only some parts, you can't, you must restart from the beginning.

When you accept the fact that you'll mostly play an interactive story more than do some detective work, [b]Orwell is pretty great[/b]. The visual, the global atmosphere is really spot-on for the theme. The music helps a lot (and it shows this is really a story, as the music changes the second you find some important stuff). There are a few twists, and despite the lack of decision-making and all, I liked a lot how the story was told and how I seemingly was the one unfolding it.
The story is good. The click and drag simulator mechanics make it boring.

Short but sweet; you can definitely finish this game in about three to four hours.  It has some replay value if you want to get more achievements and different endings, but there isn't as much value to it as the first play through.

I recommend purchasing this on sale as it is short, but I don't have any complaints about the controls or how it ran on my PC.  Everything went smoothly and I fell deep into the game-finished it in one sitting since I had the time.

Suspenseful, fun, easy to learn, and story rich.
10/10 would ruin people's lives time and time again!

This. Game. Is. Amazing. I got so into this game, I played it all in one sitting. It constantly keeps you guessing and you can be sure there is a curve ball around every corner. The story and the world are very interesting and the game mechanics are easy to pick up. Every action you take hold weight as it has a significant impact on the outcome of the game. Highly recommend playing this game, especially if you like sotry driven games.

Overall a decent story, although I went into it kind of hoping for a few standalone crime-solving missions where I could be a dick and falsely implicate people, or pry deeply into aspects of peoples lives that were irrelevant to the case. Y'know, stuff that would say a lot about the perils of an all-seeing state spying apparatus. Ah well, would still recommend it.
Never has a game intrigued me as much as this.

Stop what you're doing.

Stop reading this and buy the game. Now.

For 10 bucks? (I got it for 8 on sale though) This immersive experience is going to blow your mind (pardon the overused euphemism) but really. Wow. This was an absolutely fantastic ride. I do not regret spending my money on this game whatsoever! I think that, given some exposure on both Youtube and elsewhere, this game could get big! And it should! It's absolutely fantastic! I love the art style personally, but hey, that's personal taste.

Let me tell you precisely what you're getting so this review isn't just screaming praise about this game.

While the mechanics are beyond simple, (click various articles and search them for relevant data) it makes you feel really uneasy about delving into people's personal lives, about what it feels like to be in places you REALLY shouldn't be. 

All of the choices you make, each little piece of information you submit, can come back to bite you in the ass. Hard. If I have any tips for new players, don't just submit everything, ESPECIALLY conflicting data!!!! Make sure to read all bits of information and all of the articles in full before you submit everything! That's not just flavor text around the submittable parts, ALL OF IT IS IMPORTANT! And that's really what I like about this game- there's nothing gone to waste. Nothing that's just hopeless. All 'dead ends' are just waiting for the right door to open with another bit of text. It's nerve wracking and I LOVE it! 

I have no regrets on this game whatsoever. I'm more than happy that I bought it and I can't wait to see more (hopefully more excellent storytelling like in this game!) from the Devs. Really now, if you like story based games like the Telltale series of games, absolutely pick this up. What it lacks in mechanics it ABSOLUTELY makes up for in story, atmosphere, tension, and replayability! I'll be starting another playthrough shortly.

i got this game because i liked one of the other games the developer has made. it took a bit for me to get going but once i did i couldn't stop playing i was drawn to find out what would happen and just when i think i got it all figuered out something would happen and i find myself puzzling all the other decisions i made that led up to it i totaly recomend this game

Just finished this beautiful, beautiful game.

I can't say enough good things about it. From the subtle and gorgeous music, to the crisp and stylized artwork, to the streamlined "browser" interface of the game design, to the brilliant and immersive writing... this game is just a work of art.

If you're a fan of "decisions matter" games, especially ones with a "human vs. government" aspect like "Papers, Please", or if you're just in the mood for what's essentially a gorgeous interactive novel, you need this game. As other reviewers have said, don't watch gameplay vids, don't read about the story, just play it. It's worth the money.

It's been a long time since a game captured me so completely. The twists and turns and gradual unwinding of the plot happen at such a perfect pace. There were times I burst out laughing, times I was actually brought to tears, and even half a chapter where I sat with one hand over my mouth as I clicked through with the other. Now I can't wait to play it again to make different choices and see how things play out.

10/10 would happily subject myself to emotional battery again.
Great, engaging story. Definitely recommend!
This game is amazing. The most entranced I have ever been in a choice based game. Just amazing!

Fantastic game, I can't praise it enough. Solid story, solid characters and character progression, appealing art style, and perfect general pacing. The soundtrack, works perfectly for it- being that it's essentially a solid, subtle repeat throughout the entire game really makes those times where it picks up stand out and feel that much more important.  I really, really hope to see more from this company. And, admittedly, would love it if this premise is revisited in some way. This is the best game I've played in a long, long time. Exactly what I've been looking for. I just couldn't stop playing. I'm kind of sad that I've completely finished it. 

Issues; 
Some of the dialogue becomes a bit broken depending on your choices. Oftentimes Symes and Delacroix mentioned information that I'd intentionally not given them, later on in the story. This only really becomes noticeable on replay-but it could be worked on. Nothing like this will ever be perfect--I'm never going to seriously complain about a choice game having little issues like this. There's just too much that would have to go into a game with so many variants it to make it possible. 
There were a few lingering spelling/grammatical errors, which, given the nature of the game (Internet, instant messaging/texting), didn't really bother me all that much. (Such as Harrison tried to "fell" instead of flee.) I see these things on real articles, it's no different.
There are some bugs present, but, they're clearly being revised and, honestly, aren't game-breaking at this point.

My personal ideas; I believe there could be a little work done on the pacing of the listener- real-time DOES make it all that much more immersive, but, when it comes to replayabilty, and just the general idea of it most likely having an adult player-base, who may only have an hour or so to play before going back to their day-to-day, I feel like there should be...maybe an additional option in the settings to modify speed or..something? It's easier, and more fulfilling to put a game down for a session if you feel you were able to hit a certain level of 'achievement.' You know, the pleasure centers of the brain and all. Maybe if it were simply a more fluid letter-by-letter or syllabalic instead of by completion of a word? I don't know. 
The only other thing I could possibly suggest, would be for, if ever this title is revisited or turned into a 'series' of sorts, that it be a little more flexible? The ability to freely investigate more than is necessary--even additional people. Perhaps just in a casual sense aside from the story, since there is a necessary feeling of a 'time pinch' in the game itself. I think a lot of the audience are people like me who just like to dig, so the chance to just..index on a larger scale would be quite entertaining. 
And, lastly, the ability to generate more datachunks? This could be messy territory, though. I think this would fall into the 'would require too much forethought to ever be possible' category, but it's an idea nontheless. The system is automated, clearly, but, the evaluator should have an option to deem other things appropriate for investigation. I know there were a few things that I would have loved to have flagged that just weren't an option.

My apologies, I'm just VERY excited and passionate about this title. Guys, play it!

What to say about this game....

You play as a loyal outsourced investigator for "The Nation", and their new security program called Orwell.  The Orwell program is essentially surveillance designed to "keep the people of the Nation safe."  You investigate a group of individuals in an attempt to determine the culprit of a series of terrorist attacks.  Armed with the most invasive software at your disposal, you use every tool to spy on, and hopefully locate, all of the responsible parties.

Personally, it took me some time to get past the eerie feeling that what I was doing to spy on the lives of these virtual people wasn't too far off from what's probably been taking place in the world for a number of years.  This aspect of the game alone can make you feel almost uncomfortable with what you are doing.  However, your contact within Orwell does well, reminding you that what you are doing is for the safety of all.

The game itself, while it is a reading game at heart, does a really good job of pulling you in.  There are plot twists galore, and the game leaves you wanting to see the next piece of information you can dig up.

TL;DR - If you enjoy a dystopian setting, and enjoy reading-intensive games/mysteries, then I think you'll enjoy this game.  It is a short game; only a few hours, but it is definitely worth a few bucks.  I personally hope that they can use this to make a sequel of some kind.

Absolutely adore this game. It's intriguing and engaging, not too difficult but still clever. The game uses music effectively to set the mood for different events and it's overall an incredible game even though the mechanics are so simple.

From the moment I saw the trailer on the store page, to the moment I finished all 5 chapters, I became a commited investigator. THis is my first review so bear with me...

I've played a many story games within my life, but I never found one so gutwrenching and enjoyable as this one. The game itself isn't very hard, and I was able to complete one of the endings in a little under four hours, but those four hours had me biting my nails and staying up intil 2 in the morning. This game makes you feel like you are watching actual people, stalking their every move and finding out about their personal life. This game also makes you reflect on how much should be wary of a government watch in the world today, and what that means for a society with such elaborate spying skills.

I wont say anything, but the ending is absolut genius as it has multiple options and suprises you in many ways. My advice, don't be cheap and watch this on Youtube, BUY THIS GAME, sit in a dark corner with nothing to bother and play this game from start to finish. I garuntee you it'll be worth your while.

Excellent game.

To those who know the references and like the source material this game is based off of, this is perhaps the best Big Brother/Orwellian Surveillance system simulator I've seen so far, and is well worth the price its asking for. 

Fans of Papers, Please will probably enjoy this game just as much. Except instead of being the Border Crossing Guard, think of yourself as the Investigator for their Surveillance Corps.

Its a short game, sure, you can beat it once probably within 4 hours, but it does have some replayability (plus the fact that there is no hard save points, the game constantly saves after everything you do with no way of going back outside of making a new profile, so it forces you to choose wisely). To me, the shortness is forgiveable for how much this game costs (which isn't much).

The writing is amazing for it being a game with only written dialogue, the characters feel real and individual and you're the spider trying to weave out the web of how they fit into the plot that's going on. It also does a great job of getting you into the role of being an Investigator of a secret service public spying agency, you feel as if you're in the game just as much as any of them at times.

The art style is consistent and works for the game that this is, but IMO they could have had clear photos and models and you would have had the same game, this style merely gives it a more individual feel rather than it being like any other game like this.

The gameplay is simple, but great if you're into investigative puzzle-solving.

The music is very good for eliciting responses and making you feel certain emotions at particular times, as its supposed to, though IMO it moves a little too fast at times in transitions. You're often left with an abrupt music cue and wondering "What the hell, what did I just find?" before you can properly read what found. But otherwise its good.

Only encountered one bug at the very end of the game where it froze and looped the last second or two of the music track I was listening to, and I had to exit out with alt-tab, but I had beaten the playthrough by that point so it wasn't a huge deal.

All and all, a great game for the price its asking for, and if you're a fan of the type of genre this is.

This game is a thought-provoking foray into the concept of the Orwellian panopticon of many distopian fiction.  It cronicles the choices that you, as an investigator, make in the resolution of a terrorism investigation.  If you enjoy games like [u]Papers, Please[/u] and Telltale Games' [u]Wolf Among Us[/u], you'll definitely like this game.  I had doubts about the tesselated graphics (they are remeniscent of the original  [u]Flashback[/u]), but they primarily only serve as avatars in the web-of-knowledge that you construct as part of the investigation.

Some have complained about the idea of the game being...simplistic; however, the game seems to have a decent number of branches depending on which of the pieces of intel you select and (importantly) [i]when you select them[/i].  I haven't begun to explore all of the nodes of the decision tree, but with each of the paths that I've traversed I only want to know more of the story.  Is there an ultimate [b]truth[/b]?  I must know.

tl;dr BUY IT FOR YOUR HEALTH AND YOUR NATION'S HEALTH

Just finished Orwell. 

Honestly I'm blown away, the myriad of choices you're given and how much they actually matter to the story and what happens floored me. The game is about a dystopian style future where everything is under surveilance and you're the one behind the camera. The story is amazing and definitely engaging, more than one playthrough guaranteed. I've seen this done with other games but honestly the execution of Orwell is great. 

SO MUCH INFORMATION - Useful info and completely worthless info, both can drastically impact your game. Input the wrong info and you may screw yourself over. 

UNNATURAL RELATIONSHIPS - You will either love or hate digital characters you have no real connection with.... and then feel bad about decisions you make based on your feelings towards them. 

I will literally be talking about this game for another week just from one singular outcome. My anticipation for the next playthrough is through the roof right now. I'd be playing it again now if I wasn't trying to process my last playthrough currently.

Also please do not let the play-time scare you away, despite the low time this game is worth every penny. I haven't been this engrossed in a game for a very long time. I kept thinking well I can put it down for a bit and come back later, but I couldn't bring myself to put it down.

Overall this game was good. I would'nt give this game a 10/10 for a couple reasons however for under ten dollars, I would purchase and plkay the game.

A poignant game on the times we live in. I'm a humongous fan of the "Walking Simulator" genre and I stumbled upon this game during the Steam Winter Sale (3 days ago). Orwell has a captivating storyline that takes the "first person" experience quite literally. Without spoiling the game, the story focuses on a user operated software called Orwell, where the player assumes the role as a operator outside the fictatious "Nation", spying on activists that are tagged as potentially violent. 

The user interface is streamlined, dare I say "user-friendly". The fictional profiles depicted in the video game are unnervingly real, pulling me into the experience, as though as I really am spying on others. The characters are well scripted, albeit being scripts of text. The characters are caricatures of stereotypical activists, with complex backgrounds and hidden agendas. 

The "orwellian" connotations that are hinted at in the game are subtle, nuanced without being too overbearing or obvious. As you progressively submit information on labelled targets, you start to feel a heavy burden of responsibility on your shoulders. The multiple options and consequences from submitting false information add more weight to the situation. The activities or rituals performed by the main character are a frighteningly realistic, depecting the state of the world we live in. 

My only complaints include the duration of the game: it is rather short in length, more like a concept game showcasing some of the developer's strengths. The waiting times between each mission is abysmal, sometimes resulting in multiple crashes. 

All in all, this is an underrated gem in the walking simulator category, standing tall with the likes of Gone Home and Soma.

This seemed like a novel and interesting title when I first found it. After playing through I can say this is so much more.

When you talk about games that move you people might say things like Mass Effect, Deus Ex, and various other story based games, or if we look at the indie side of thing you will get: Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons, This War of Mine, and To the Moon.

I can tell you this game does it just as effectively, if not more so, because YOU -- the actual you sitting at your computer -- are a charter in the game. Add that to the decisions you have to make and the pressures you will feel -- even though it's just  a game -- it will make you react to the story almost as though it is real.

You will care about what is happening, deeply.

You will be unable to stop, just like with a good book.

And all that's just the story, this game is also basically a case study of a surveillance state, like in the book 1984 (as you might have guessed from the title of the game) and references to the book are goddamn everywhere.

So, should you buy it? IMO yes you should it is an amazing experience.
If you like visual novels (Ace Attorney comes to mind) you will love this. (as it basicly is one)
If you like a good book you will love this.
If you like just a good story you will love this

And for that reason, should you consider ever buying this, I vehemently urge you to go in completely blind -- if you haven't read the description about this game on steam, don't. This game is better the less you know of  what is going on when you start, and if you spoil it all the magic will be lost.

However should you come here expecting a good "GAMING" experience and you care little for the story you will be very disappointed with this game as gameplay is as simple if not more than many of the classic flash games on sites like addictinggames.

I give it a 9/10 though it pains me to do so

I just can't give it a perfect to to some niggles in the interface that are simply annoying.

Regardless you should play this game (try the demo, it's part of the actual game not some curated bull crap like ubisoft does)
